nodes.name: Solvothermal synthesis of PtTe₂ NRs
nodes.procedure: Pt(acac)₂ (5.0 mg), K₂TeO₃ (6.0 mg), PVP (100.0 mg), C₂H₆O₂ (20.0 mg) were dissolved in ethylene glycol (10.0 mL). Then, the mixture was magnetically stirred until a homogeneous solution was formed. After that, the homogeneous mixture solution was then transferred into a Teflon-sealed autoclave and maintained at 180°C for 3 h. After cooling to room temperature, the PtTe₂ NRs were collected by centrifugation and washed three times with ethanol/acetone solution.

nodes.name: Carbon support loading of PtTe₂ NRs
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared PtTe₂ NRs were dispersed in ethanol (10.0 mL) and then Vulcan XC-72 carbon powders were added to the above suspension. After sonication for 30 min, the PtTe₂ NRs/C was collected by centrifugation and washed several times using ethanol/acetone solution. The obtained PtTe₂ NRs/C was vacuum-dried for further use.

nodes.source_text: 2.3. Preparation of Pt/PtTeₓ NRs/C The as-prepared PtTe₂ NRs were dispersed in ethanol (10.0 mL) and then Vulcan XC-72 carbon powders were added ... vacuum-dried for further use.

nodes.name: Electrochemical activation to Pt/PtTeₓ NRs/C
nodes.procedure: To prepare Pt/PtTeₓ NRs/C, 2.0 mg PtTe₂ NRs/C was dispersed in the mixture solution containing 200 μL IPA and 5 μL Nafion (5 wt%) and then sonicated for 1 h to get the homogeneous ink. After that, 5 μL of the ink was cast onto the glassy carbon electrode (GCE) with a diameter of 5 mm and vacuum-dried. Finally, the Pt/PtTeₓ NRs/C was prepared by cyclic voltammetry (CV) for certain cycles in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ at room temperature. The obtained Pt/PtTeₓ NRs/C was scraped from the electrode by ultrasonication in ethanol, followed by centrifugation and vacuum-dry for further characterization.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals hollow nanorod morphology of PtTe2 NRs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As revealed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) ... the as-synthesized products show the outline of hollow nanorods (Figs. 1a and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.290 nm for PtTe2 (101) planes and polycrystalline nature (SAED).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The precise micromorphology of PtTe2 NRs was investigated by high-resolution TEM (HRTEM). As shown in Fig. 1b, distinct lattice fringes are observed ... The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of PtTe2 NRs exhibits some distinct diffraction rings.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM with EDS mapping shows Pt and Te elements overlap uniformly along PtTe2 NRs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM elemental mappings of PtTe2 NRs show that Pt and Te elements overlap well along the NRs (Fig. 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS shows Pt/Te atomic ratio of 35.5:64.7 for PtTe2 NRs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt/Te atomic ratio of the product is determined to be around 1:2 by both energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) (Pt/Te = 35.5:64.7) (Fig. S3a).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms Pt/Te ratio of 32.9:67.1 for PtTe2 NRs and 59.0:41.0 for Pt/PtTe_x NRs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt/Te atomic ratio of the product is determined to be around 1:2 by both energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) (Pt/Te = 35.5:64.7) (Fig. S3a) and inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) (Pt/Te = 32.9:67.1).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows typical peaks of PtTe2 (JCPDS No. 18-0977) for PtTe2 NRs; new Pt phase appears for Pt/PtTe_x NRs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) pattern of the product shows the typical peaks of PtTe2 (JCPDS No. 18-0977) ... Compared to the PXRD pattern of the pristine PtTe2 NRs, a new Pt phase appears on the PXRD pattern of the Pt/PtTe_x NRs.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.227 nm [Pt(111)] and 0.289 nm [PtTe2(101)] with distinct Pt/PtTe_x heterojunction interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image of Pt/PtTe_x NRs exhibits distinct lattice fringes of Pt and PtTe2, where the lattice spacing of 0.227 and 0.289 nm were ascribed to Pt(111) plane and PtTe2(101) plane, respectively ... distinct interfaces between Pt(111) and PtTe2(101) are observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM-EDS mappings show Pt-rich, Te-less uniform distribution along Pt/PtTe_x NRs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM-EDS elemental mappings of Pt/PtTe_x NRs show that Pt-rich and Te-less elements are uniformly distributed along the NRs due to Te dissolution (Fig. 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS shows Pt/Te atomic ratio of 62.5:37.5 for Pt/PtTe_x NRs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt/PtTe_x NRs show the Pt/Te atomic ratio of 62.5:37.5 (Fig. S3b), consistent with the ICP-OES value of Pt/Te = 59.0:41.0.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Pt(0)/Pt(II) peak area ratio increases from 0.11 for PtTe2 NRs to 1.71 for Pt/PtTe_x NRs; Pt(0) binding energy shifts -0.4 eV vs Pt/C; Te(IV) shifts +1.0 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak area ratio of Pt(0)/Pt(II) increases from 0.11 of PtTe2 NRs to 1.71 of Pt/PtTe_x NRs ... Compared with Pt/C, Pt/PtTe_x NRs exhibit a negative shift of 0.4 eV in the binding energy of Pt(0) ... The Te(IV) peak of Pt/PtTe_x NRs shows a positive shift of 1.0 eV compared with that of PtTe2 NRs.

nodes.characterization_summary: CO stripping reveals ECSA of 78 m²/g_Pt for Pt/PtTe_x NRs (vs 56 m²/g_Pt for Pt/C) and 1.4× more active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ECSA of Pt/PtTe_x NRs (78 m² g⁻¹ Pt) is much larger than that of Pt/C (56 m² g⁻¹ Pt) ... the number of active sites of Pt/PtTe_x NRs is 1.4 times that of Pt/C.
